title: Build a Bitcask Log-Structured Store
summary:
Build Bitcask, the storage engine behind Riak, on real files. You write **append-only data files** of CRC-checked records, an in-memory **keydir** so every read is a single positioned read, **tombstone** deletes, **file rotation** at a size limit, **merge/compaction** that writes **hint files**, **crash recovery** that truncates a torn final record, and a configurable **fsync policy**.

This is the simplest real storage engine, and it teaches the ideas behind WAL and LSM interview questions: why sequential writes are fast, what `fsync` actually buys you, how you detect a torn write, why tombstones exist, and why compaction must never resurrect deleted keys. Everything runs under an injected temp directory.

milestones.name: M1: Record format
milestones.description: `encodeRecord` / `decodeRecord`: big-endian header (crc32, keyLen, valueLen), UTF-8 keys, tombstone marker; detect truncation and CRC corruption.

milestones.name: M2: Append-only store
milestones.description: put / get / keys over an append-only file and an in-memory keydir. Overwrites append and never rewrite. Data survives reopen.

milestones.name: M3: Deletes
milestones.description: Tombstones are appended only for existing keys, and deleted keys stay deleted after reopen.

milestones.name: M4: Rotation
milestones.description: Rotate the active file before it would exceed `maxFileBytes`; oversized records get their own file; reads find the right file and offset after many rotations.

milestones.name: M5: Merge and hint files
milestones.description: Compaction keeps only live values, shrinks disk use, writes one hint per output, and never resurrects deleted keys. Reopen uses the hints.

milestones.name: M6: Crash recovery and integrity
milestones.description: Truncate a torn or corrupt tail in the last file; refuse corruption in older files; verify the CRC on every read.

milestones.name: M7: Durability policy
milestones.description: fsync `always` / `never` / every N writes, counted in stats; all files stay inside the injected directory.
